$comment: Stable check specifications. The integration contract between Causeway and any engine that executes it. See gate/gate-configuration.md §11.
$authority: This file defines WHAT each check means and WHAT INPUT it needs. profiles.json defines WHERE each one blocks. An engine needs both.

input_classes.$comment: The capability handshake is compositional: an engine declares which input classes it can supply, not which checks it knows. A required check whose input class is unsupported resolves to `unsupported` and blocks. Adding a check that reuses an existing class costs an engine nothing.
input_classes.system-record: The system's registry record — tier, criticality_class, spine block, composition state.
input_classes.gate-config: The per-system ato-gate.json — exclusions, named approvers, thresholds, path overrides.
input_classes.sbom: A parsed CycloneDX or SPDX document for the build under evaluation.
input_classes.baseline: The approved SBOM baseline for the system.
input_classes.ta-record: The Tactical Authorization record, including renewal_count.
input_classes.catalog: Catalog item records and the inheritance graph.
input_classes.evidence-store: The system's evidence directory — emitted receipts and run records.
input_classes.ci-results: Results of the product repository's own test and contract suites.
input_classes.repo-lock: The .causeway-lock file in the product repository working tree.
input_classes.repo-decisions: The product repository's decisions/ directory, with ADR frontmatter parsed.
input_classes.repo-tree: Arbitrary read access to the product repository working tree.
input_classes.repo-manifests: Dependency manifests, lockfiles and ecosystem configuration in the working tree.
input_classes.repo-changeset: The set of files changed by the proposed change, with git rename and deletion scoring.
input_classes.repo-git: Repository git metadata — tags of either kind, annotated or lightweight, and their dates. Tag topology stopped being load-bearing at gate configuration v0.7: what an engine reads is a tag matching the release pattern, and which kind it was is recorded as release_proof rather than filtered on.

verdicts.$comment: The result vocabulary an engine must implement. `error` and `unsupported` are distinct from `fail` on purpose: a check that could not run has not found anything, and reporting it as a finding is how a broken evaluator reads as a clean build.

waived.meaning: Violated, but covered by a valid unexpired waiver ADR. Recorded in the receipt.

not_applicable.meaning: The check's applicability rule excludes this system or this change.

not_run.meaning: Not in the inventory at this profile. Distinct from not_applicable, which means it was in scope and did not apply.

advisory.meaning: Evaluated and violated, at a profile where this check files a finding.

unsupported.meaning: The engine cannot supply an input class this check requires. Blocks when the check is blocking at this profile.

error.meaning: The check could not execute reliably. Blocks when the check is blocking at this profile.

waiver_forms.adr-waiver: A waiver ADR under the project's decisions/ directory, with a named approver and a mandatory expiry.
waiver_forms.gate-exclusion: A dated entry in ato-gate.json exclusions[]. For checks measuring the wrong thing rather than finding a real gap.
waiver_forms.none: Not waiverable at any profile. The sentence a waiver would have to commit somebody to is one nobody signs.

checks.title: SBOM ingest and drift
checks.question: Does the build's component inventory match the approved baseline?
checks.description: Parses the build's SBOM and compares it against the system's approved baseline. Components added, removed or version-shifted since the baseline are drift.
checks.remediation: Re-baseline deliberately with the gate's baseline subcommand, or revert the unintended dependency change. A baseline moved without review is drift that stopped being reported.

checks.title: Secrets scan
checks.question: Are there credentials committed to the working tree?
checks.description: Scans the repository for committed secrets — keys, tokens, connection strings with embedded credentials.
checks.remediation: Remove the secret, rotate it, and move it to the runtime secret store named in the system's SA-5.5 ADR. Removing it from the working tree does not rotate it.

checks.title: Named approver present
checks.question: Does every named-approver row carry a person's name?
checks.description: The eight † rows in the spine require a named human approver, not a role. This check verifies each closing ADR's frontmatter carries a name and a role.
checks.remediation: Add an approver block to the ADR frontmatter with a person's name and role. A role alone does not close a † row — the point is that somebody specific accepted the consequence.

checks.title: As-built notification
checks.question: Where an ADR declares ongoing unrecoverable exposure, was somebody told?
checks.description: When a revision adds a one-way row to a system already in production, the closing ADR states the as-built answer. Where that answer declares ongoing unrecoverable exposure, the ISSM is notified and the ADR records who and when.
checks.remediation: Complete the as_built.notified block with a person, a role and a date. The check verifies the record exists; it cannot verify the conversation happened.

checks.title: Waiver expiry
checks.question: Is any waiver or gate exclusion past its expiry date?
checks.description: Every waiver ADR and every ato-gate.json exclusion carries a mandatory expiry. This check fails when one has passed.
checks.remediation: Close the underlying row, or renew the waiver with a fresh expiry and a named approver. Exit code 2 is deliberately distinct from 1 so dashboards can separate rot from regression.

checks.title: Dependency provenance
checks.question: Is every dependency resolved from a committed lockfile with integrity hashes?
checks.description: Discovers the ecosystems present from the manifests in the working tree. Each must have a committed lockfile alongside it, carrying integrity hashes for every resolved entry, with no dependency resolving from a floating range at build time.
checks.applicability: not_applicable when the repository declares no third-party dependencies. Vendored trees pass on the vendored content rather than on a lockfile.
checks.remediation: Commit the lockfile your package manager already generates. Where the lockfile format omits integrity hashes, enable them — every major ecosystem supports it.

checks.title: Install-script execution disabled
checks.question: Can third-party code execute on the build runner at dependency install time?
checks.description: npm/yarn/pnpm require ignore-scripts in committed config AND an explicit --ignore-scripts on the CI invocation — both, because either alone is one edit away from silence. pip installs must resolve to wheels. No curl-pipe-shell or equivalent unverified bootstrap in a build step.
checks.applicability: not_applicable for ecosystems with no install-time execution — Go modules, Maven, NuGet. An N/A here reports that SA-5.14 was answered well.
checks.remediation: Set ignore-scripts in the committed ecosystem config and pass it explicitly in CI. Replace any curl-pipe-shell bootstrap with a pinned, checksum-verified download.
checks.non_waiverable_because: A waiver would have to read 'arbitrary third-party code may execute on our CI runners until a date,' and nobody who reads that sentence signs it.

checks.title: Short-form closure
checks.question: Do all 23 short-form rows have closing ADRs?
checks.description: The 23 rows in the short form are owed by every system at every criticality class. This check verifies each has an ADR with an accepted status.
checks.remediation: Run the Decision Spine skill against the repository. It scopes to the system's class and produces a Decision Register naming exactly what is open.

checks.title: Composition state declared
checks.question: Is the system declared catalog-composed, wrapped, or unmanaged?
checks.description: Verifies system.json declares a composition state from the closed set. Composition against the catalog is what earns inherited control credit, so an undeclared state means inheritance cannot be resolved.
checks.remediation: Set composition-state in system.json to one of the three values. Wrapping is a legitimate and permanently acceptable answer; declaring a wrapped system catalog-composed is not.
checks.engine_contract_note: Bumped to 2 in standard 1.6.0. The valid value set changed — see ADR 0008. An engine reporting contract 1 for this check is reading the pre-1.6.0 answer set.

checks.title: Mapped control checks
checks.question: Do the 800-53 controls the profile requires have passing evidence?
checks.description: Runs the control checks mapped by the system's profile and overlay, and reports which controls have failing evidence.
checks.remediation: Each failing control names its own evidence gap. Inherited controls resolve through the catalog rather than through this system.

checks.title: One-way door closure
checks.question: Are all 28 one-way rows closed?
checks.description: One-way decisions are expensive or impossible to reverse. The spine's deadline is before production code — stated in spine.md, AGENTS.md and the decision-spine skill. The gate reads G1 and above as production code existing, because a Tactical Authorization and a sandbox tenant mean a deployed system, and that is why this warns at G0 and blocks above. It verifies each row has a closing ADR. It does not read release_state, and never did. See ADR 0034.
checks.remediation: Close the open one-way rows. The spine's deadline is before production code, so at G1 and above they are already late; they stay owed and get more expensive with every commit built on them. Rows a spine revision added after this system shipped close against the adoption horizon, which is what the modifier on this cell is for.
checks.engine_contract_note: Unchanged at v0.8 on purpose. The verdict logic did not move — this check has blocked unconditionally at G1 and above since v0.1, and release_state was evidence it never read. What moved is the declared input set, and only downward: every engine that could run this check before still can. See ADR 0034.

checks.title: Class-scoped closure
checks.question: Are all rows in scope for this system's criticality class closed?
checks.description: Scopes the spine to the system's criticality class — 23 rows at C3, 89 at C2, 94 at C1 — and verifies each in-scope row has a closing ADR.
checks.remediation: Run the Decision Spine skill. A missing criticality_class resolves to C1 and puts all 94 rows in scope, which is the loud default and usually the actual cause.

checks.title: Waiver horizon
checks.question: Is any waiver expiring within 60 days?
checks.description: Surfaces waivers approaching expiry at every profile, so the deadline arrives as a sequence of warnings rather than as a build failure nobody saw coming.
checks.remediation: Close the underlying row or renew the waiver before it expires and turns into an exit code 2.

checks.title: Tests accompany source changes
checks.question: Did a change touching source also touch tests?
checks.description: Partitions the changed-file set into source, test and neither. Generated and vendored paths count as neither. Subtracts pure deletions and renames git scores at 100% similarity, leaving source_effective. Fires when source_effective is non-empty and the test set is empty.
checks.applicability: not_applicable when no source files changed, or when source_effective is empty after the two subtractions.
checks.remediation: Add tests covering the changed behavior. Where the test suite lives in a different repository the check is measuring the wrong changed-file set — that is the legitimate gate-exclusion case, dated like every other one.

checks.title: Adoption horizon
checks.question: Is any newly-owed row's adoption horizon expiring within 60 days?
checks.description: Mirrors waiver-horizon-60d exactly, for rows that became owed when the system's pinned standard moved ahead of its spine.closed_against.
checks.applicability: not_applicable when spine.closed_against is absent — a system with no recorded closure point has no grace to expire.
checks.remediation: Close the newly-owed rows before their horizon expires. The clock is anchored to the release date of the revision that added the row, so re-syncing does not move it.

checks.title: Standard currency
checks.question: How old is the pinned copy of the standard?
checks.description: Measures the pinned copy's age from the released= line in .causeway-lock. Age, not distance behind current — age is computable from the lock alone, with no network and no assumption that the standard's repository is reachable.
checks.remediation: Re-run sync.sh from the current standard. A system that genuinely cannot re-sync — a frozen ATO, an air-gapped release train — takes a dated gate-exclusion instead.
checks.config_error_when: The lock has no released= line. That is a lock predating standard 1.3.0; re-syncing writes it. Exit code 4.

checks.title: Sandbox tenant assigned
checks.question: Does this tactical system have a sandbox tenant?
checks.description: Operational-tier systems under Tactical Authorization run in an assigned sandbox tenant. This check verifies the assignment exists and matches the deploy target.
checks.applicability: G1 only. not_applicable at other profiles.
checks.remediation: Assign a sandbox tenant in system.json, or correct the deploy target. A tactical system deploying outside its sandbox is the failure mode the tier exists to prevent.

checks.title: Tactical Authorization valid and unexpired
checks.question: Is the Tactical Authorization active?
checks.description: Verifies the TA record exists, is issued by a TAO on the roster, and has not expired or been revoked.
checks.applicability: G1 only. not_applicable at other profiles.
checks.remediation: Renew the TA through the issuance workflow, or let it sunset. Sunset is the default state for a tactical system, not an exception.

checks.title: Promote-or-sunset
checks.question: Has a system on its third TA term decided whether to promote or sunset?
checks.description: Operational + C1 forces a promote-or-sunset decision at TA expiry. Passes at renewal_count 0, warns at 1, and blocks at 2 or more unless disposition_ref resolves to an Accepted ADR.
checks.applicability: tier == operational AND criticality_class == C1. not_applicable otherwise.
checks.remediation: Record a promotion to mission tier, or a sunset ADR with a date, and reference it in tactical_authorization.disposition_ref. Sunset is a legitimate disposition — the rule is decide, not promote.
checks.engine_note: renewal_count lives on the TA record and is incremented by the issuance workflow, never by the build. Rebuilding, forking or re-running CI must not move it.

checks.title: Control inheritance resolves
checks.question: Does every inherited control resolve to a provider that actually implements it?
checks.description: Walks parent-system-id, inherits-from and catalog-composition to resolve the inheritance graph, and fails on any inherited control with no resolving provider.
checks.remediation: Correct the inheritance declaration, or implement the control locally. An unresolved inherited control is a control nobody implements that everybody believes is covered.

checks.title: Evidence pipeline emitting
checks.question: Is the system producing evidence on a current cadence?
checks.description: Verifies the evidence store has receipts recent enough to show the pipeline is live rather than historical.
checks.remediation: Wire the gate into CI so it runs on every push. Evidence generated by hand on request is the state this check exists to detect.

checks.title: Contract tests green
checks.question: Do the consumer contract tests pass?
checks.description: Reads the product repository's contract test results and fails on any red suite.
checks.applicability: not_applicable when the system exposes no consumer-facing contract.
checks.remediation: Fix the contract or version it. A backward-compatibility guarantee with a red contract suite behind it is not a guarantee.

checks.title: DR plan of record exists
checks.question: Is there an accepted ADR stating the DR posture?
checks.description: Verifies SA-7.4 is closed with an accepted ADR naming the DR posture.
checks.remediation: Close SA-7.4 with an ADR naming backup-restore, active-passive or active-active, and what it costs.

checks.title: DR drill within cadence
checks.question: Has a DR drill happened inside the stated cadence?
checks.description: Reads the last drill record and compares it against the cadence the system's SA-7.5 ADR declares.
checks.applicability: not_applicable when the DR posture is backup-restore with no failover path.
checks.remediation: Run the drill and record it. A DR plan never exercised is a document, not a capability.

checks.title: Exposure review current
checks.question: Has the system's outward exposure been reviewed inside its cadence?
checks.description: Reads the catalog record's exposure review date against the system's review cadence.
checks.applicability: G3 only. not_applicable at other profiles.
checks.remediation: Conduct the exposure review and update the catalog record. Core-tier systems expose the most and change the least, which is exactly why the cadence exists.

checks.title: Promotion review current
checks.question: Has the system's promotion path been reviewed inside its cadence?
checks.description: Reads the catalog record's promotion review date against the system's review cadence.
checks.applicability: G3 only. not_applicable at other profiles.
checks.remediation: Conduct the promotion review and update the catalog record.

checks.title: AO signature on SA-5.10
checks.question: Has the Authorizing Official signed the SA-5.10 decision?
checks.description: SA-5.10 requires an AO signature in the closing ADR's frontmatter, not merely a named approver.
checks.remediation: Obtain the AO signature and record the name, role and date in the ADR frontmatter.
